Spatial Operators

class ibfs.spatial_operators.SpatialOperators(Re: float, mesh: Mesh, bcs: Tuple[BoundaryConditions], test: bool | None = False)[source]

Bases: object

Class to evaluate the right-hand side of the Navier-Stokes equation.

Parameters:

  • Re (float) – Reynolds number

  • mesh (Mesh) – an instance of the Mesh class

  • bcs (Tuple[BoundaryConditions]) – a tuple of instances of the BoundaryConditions class (the length of the tuple is equal to the number of velocity components)

assemble_divergence_matrix()[source]

Instantiate the attribute self.D, containing the matrix representation of the divergence operator defined in evaluate_divergence().

assemble_gradient_matrix()[source]

Instantiate the attribute self.G, containing the matrix representation of the gradient operator defined in evaluate_gradient().

assemble_laplacian_matrix()[source]

Instantiate the attribute self.L, containing the matrix representation of the pressure laplacian operator \(L = D G\), where \(D\) and \(G\) are the divergence and gradient operators, respectively.

augment_pressure_laplacian()[source]

The discrete laplacian \(L = DG\) (where \(D\) and \(G\) are the discrete divergence and gradient operators) is singular with a one-dimensional right nullspace spanned by \(v = const\). The left nullspace \(w\) is unknown, but can be computed easily following the approach in section 3.3 of [Padovan2021]. We then update self.L to

\[\begin{split}L_a = \begin{bmatrix} L & v \\ w^T & 0 \end{bmatrix}\end{split}\]

which is invertible.

References

[Padovan2021]

Padovan and Rowley, A computationally efficient approach for the removal of the phase shift singularity in harmonic resolvent analysis, arXiv:2102.09678, 2021

enforce_divergence_free(t, q)[source]

Compute \(q - G \Delta^{-1} D q\).

Parameters:

  • t (float) – time

  • q (xp.array) – vector containing the velocity vector at collocation points

Return type:

xp.array

evaluate_divergence() → array[source]

Compute \(\nabla\cdot \mathbf{u} = \partial_x u + \partial_y v\) at cell centers.

Return type:

xp.array

evaluate_laplacian(w: array, d: float) → array[source]

Compute \(\nabla^2 w = \left(\partial_x^2 w + \partial_y^2 w\right)\), where \(w\) is either the \(x\) or \(y\) velocity field.

Attention

This function returns an array of a different size than the original input array \(w\). If \(w\) has size \(n\times m\), the dimension of the output array will be \((n-2)\times (m-2)\).

Parameters:

  • w (xp.array) – two-dimensional array

  • d (float) – grid spacing

Return type:

cupy/numpy array

evaluate_momentum_equation() → Tuple[array, array][source]

Evaluate the discretized momentum equation (without pressure) in the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. Returns a 2-tuple containing the evaluation of the \(x\)- and \(y\)-momentum equations.

Return type:

Tuple[xp.array, xp.array]

evaluate_pressure_gradient() → Tuple[array, array][source]

Compute \(\left(\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}, \frac{\partial p}{\partial y}\right)\) at cell faces.

Return type:

Tuple[xp.array, xp.array]

evaluate_right_hand_side(t, q)[source]

Compute

\[\mathbf{r}(\mathbf{u}) = -\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla\mathbf{u} + Re^{-1}\Delta \mathbf{u} + \mathbf{f}(t)\]

where \(\mathbf{u}\) is the continuous-in-space velocity vector and \(q = (u_h, v_h) \in \mathbb{R}^n\) contains the spatially-discretized velocity vector.

Parameters:

  • t (float) – time

  • q (xp.array) – vector containing the velocity vector at collocation points

Return type:

xp.array

evaluate_streamwise_advection(u: array, v: array, d: float) → array[source]

Compute

\[\int_{Y} u^2(x,y)\big\lvert_{x=x_{l}}^{x=x_r}\,dy + \int_{X}\left[u(x,y)v(x,y)\right]_{y={y_b}}^{y=y_{t}}\,dx\]

on each finite volume (see Figure 2 in the docs/notes/cfd_solver_details.pdf).

Attention

This function returns an array of size \(n_y \times (n_x - 1)\), where \(n_y\) and \(n_x\) are the number of internal cell centers in the \(y\) and \(x\) directions, respectively.

Parameters:

  • u (xp.array) – streamwise velocity field

  • v (xp.array) – wall-normal velocity field

  • d (float) – grid spacing

Return type:

xp.array

evaluate_wallnormal_advection(u: array, v: array, d: float) → array[source]

Compute

\[\int_{X} v^2(x,y)\big\lvert_{y=y_{b}}^{y=y_t}\,dx + \int_{Y}\left[u(x,y)v(x,y)\right]_{x={x_l}}^{x=x_{t}}\,dy\]

on each finite volume (see Figure 3 in the docs/notes/cfd_solver_details.pdf).

Attention

This function returns an array of size \((n_y-1) \times n_x\), where \(n_y\) and \(n_x\) are the number of internal cell centers in the \(y\) and \(x\) directions, respectively.

Parameters:

  • u (xp.array) – streamwise velocity field

  • v (xp.array) – wall-normal velocity field

  • d (float) – grid spacing

Return type:

cupy/numpy array
